data.name: Exorcism of the Legion (Last Rites) RETIRED
data.detailed_description:
New Chapter has Released!


Acerca do jogo

The Legion returns to PC, and owners get the remake FREE

Exorcism of the Legion has been completely remade for PC as Exorcism of the Legion (Last Rites) - Final Cut. Because you own this original chapter, the remake is yours free when it launches. Wishlist the Final Cut on Steam so it lands in your library at launch:
The last rite begins soon.

This game is now delisted, but it will stay in your library for you to play. However, as a thank you, we're giving you the deluxe PC remake entirely for free. Go to the demo page, and wishlist it, and you'll get it when it releases.

Deluxe Edition now available including ALL FIVE CHAPTERS

This is what you're looking for!

Chapter 1 is being delisted as of Jan 31 2026.

reviews.review:
Thoughts and Review at the Bottom. I like to put the Pros & Cons first since a lot of people prefer to read while scrolling in Review pages

PROS : 
- A Licensed VR Title based on William Peter Blatty's "The Exorcist" series (Books & Movies)
- Amazing Environment Work. Beautiful and Creepy
- Fantastic use of audio and visual ques
- Detective Work is Fun, not too difficult and doesn't feel like a chore
- More then a few nods to long time fans of the series right out the gate
- Truly Immersive (Reading Articles in Multiple Hand writings, Blending Real World images with VR, etc)
- Easy Controls (Lots of Mechanics, but easy to utilize and remember)
- Can interact with pretty much everything that isn't nailed down

* CONS :
- Spoken Dialogue is very soft, needs some light tweaking so you don't explode your ears trying to turn up the volume for dialogue and then get hit by the scares. 
- No Subtitles (Sound is VERY important in this game, I can understand why none are active as default but the option would be nice.)
- A couple day one glitches, collision, lost hand tracking once or twice
- Some Mechanics are explained in Cursive hand writing. This is very immersive, but sometimes can be difficult to read.
- Teleport is a little Weird, Don't really like the look to location mechanic, prefer marking location with the controller then teleporting. (I know most VR users prefer other means of travel so this should only affect a few of us. I'm just grateful it's an option)

* The CONS took a little thought to be honest. For the price and how Amazing this game is, its hard to find faults, but if your going to write a Review you need to look at everything, right?

The Review -

Let me start by saying, The Exorcist, is one of my all time favorite Horror Films and I adore the series (Part 2 not so much but I digress). The original film is what sparked my love for Horror films in general, I saw the film when I was very young and it frightened me like no other film has since. So, when the announcement was made for this title, I was filled with a mix of excitement and fear. Excitement because there has never been a video game interpretation of the series before, and fear that like so many other games related to films, it would be a disaster. As I said, its my favorite film. I promise I would be the first person to call foul if the game was not done correctly.

Wolf and Wood has gone to great lengths to keep the aesthetics that made the series what it is, and what made the original so intense. From the moment you start, you are placed in an immersive horror film that many other Devs have tried to emulate, some with much less success then others. The use of audio and visual ques in this game is absolutely perfect, and I feel the Devs deserve an award for audio work alone. The environments are very well made, a little clipping here and there but that's more an issue with VR tech itself and not necessarily a fault of the Devs. The voice acting is fantastic, and none of the effects were used for a simple jump scares (which I am so very grateful for). Nothing in this game happens with out a reason, the fact that they don't use a visual effect JUST to show that they can do it, but rather make the scares and the visuals part of the story is something the original film had down to a science, and the Devs took note. 

Not to say that there are no jump scares, there are, but they flow with whats going on in the moment. Very well balanced. Also the Detective work is actually pretty fun and doesn't feel like a chore. The game flows very well as you uncover the story and things start to go south (as they do). I really felt like I was in a follow up to Exorcist 3 : Legion. You can see the attention to detail and respect for the source material all around you.

This game goes to show, that you do not need a Triple A studio to make something Amazing. In fact, I think if any other studio had tried their hand at this title, it would have been a pretty generic paint by numbers horror game. Wolf and Wood go out of their way to make this a genuine experience, regardless if you are familiar with the source material or not.

If, like me, you love the Exorcist franchise or are looking for a game that does Horror Right, that puts you inside the film, look no further. Beautiful and Creepy, I think Blatty would be proud.
